title: Claims triage agent (critical but untouched)

blocks.B2: Claims is the one domain where we hold both the policy corpus and the workflow, so the integration cost that blocks competitors is already paid.
blocks.B3: Two vendors sell generic document QA. Neither reaches the workflow. We believe the value is in the handoff to the reviewer, not in retrieval quality, which others appear to treat as the whole problem.
blocks.B4: The policy library is being re-platformed this quarter, so the indexing work is paid for either way. After it closes, we rebuild it ourselves.
blocks.C1: Claims that would have waited two days for a reviewer clear in minutes, or are escalated with a reason the handler can act on.

C2.arc: Year one, situational precedent for handlers. Year two, drafted decisions with reviewer approval. Year three, the reviewer queue is exceptions only.
C2.mvp_proves: That situational retrieval is good enough that handlers stop keeping private crib sheets.

blocks.C3: Senior reviewers. Their queue becomes exceptions only, which is a different job rather than less work.
D2: It will not decline a claim, declines always route to a person
It will not quote policy to a claimant
blocks.D3: A person always decides any settlement above the auto-settle threshold and any decline. On reaching one the agent stops, writes its reasoning, and routes to the named reviewer.
D4: Settles above threshold without an approval
Cites a policy clause that does not exist

F1.stem: Claims handlers decide with the full policy picture in front of them, in minutes rather than days.
focus_areas: Surface situational precedent at the moment of the decision
Route every exception with a reason the handler can act on
Keep every settlement decision above threshold with a person
Shrink the reviewer queue to genuine exceptions

blocks.A1: Claims handlers in first-notification, and senior reviewers who hold the exceptions queue.

A9.as_it_came: Support: ticket volume on policy questions is up 40 percent.
A9.as_product_states_it: Handlers cannot find situational precedent, so they escalate.
A9.what_changed: Symptom reframed as the underlying problem.

blocks.A3: They cannot find situational precedent across three policy documents, so hard claims escalate and sit with a reviewer for days.

A4.why: Accountable for cycle time, and carrying the escalation backlog.

blocks.A5: Handlers read three policy documents to answer one question, and keep a personal crib sheet of precedents because the policy library is not searchable by situation. A hard claim costs them forty minutes.
blocks.A6: The backlog grows with volume, and the escalation queue is already the bottleneck in the ops review.

categories.why: Recovers handling cost in the claims in scope.
We hold the policy corpus and the workflow; others hold neither.
Removes the escalation wait handlers complain about.

B00.outcome: Reduce cost-to-serve by 15 percent in FY26
B00.contribution: About a third of the gap, from the claims in scope

measures.measure: Time from claim submitted to decision
Share of handlers keeping a private crib sheet

gaps.text: No evidence reviewers would accept agent summaries.

_note: Passes every check. Exists to prove the A4-against-A7 warning fires without blocking.
